title: K-th Largest in a Stream

statement.md: A leaderboard shows the $k$-th largest trade size seen so far. After each new trade size arrives, report the $k$-th largest value among all sizes received up to that moment. Equal sizes count separately, so for sizes $5, 5, 3$ the 2nd largest is $5$.
If fewer than $k$ sizes have arrived, print `-1` for that step.

inputFormat: First line: $n$ and $k$. Second line: $n$ integers, the stream in arrival order.
outputFormat: $n$ lines. Line $i$ is the $k$-th largest of the first $i$ values, or `-1` when $i < k$.
hints: You only ever need the k largest values. A min-heap of size k keeps exactly those, with the k-th largest on top.
When a value arrives and the heap already holds k items, it matters only if it is larger than the top.

editorial.md: Maintain a min-heap holding the $k$ largest values so far. Its top is the $k$-th largest. A new value is pushed; if the heap then has more than $k$ items, the smallest is popped. Each step costs $O(\log k)$, so the whole stream costs $O(n \log k)$.

Sorting the prefix after every arrival costs $O(n^2 \log n)$. The heap works because values smaller than the current $k$-th largest can never become the $k$-th largest again: the set of the top $k$ only improves.

solutions.python:
import heapq
import sys


def main():
    tok = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, k = int(tok[0]), int(tok[1])
    heap = []  # min-heap of the k largest values so far
    out = []
    for s in tok[2:2 + n]:
        x = int(s)
        if len(heap) < k:
            heapq.heappush(heap, x)
        elif x > heap[0]:
            heapq.heapreplace(heap, x)
        out.append(str(heap[0]) if len(heap) == k else '-1')
    print('\n'.join(out))


main()
